描述_EN: by the mid ming period, a whole variety of new dragon types had begun to appear in chinese art. well potted and skilfully painted in light, clear cobalt blue, the form of the vase was current around the year 1500. the dragons are unusual, for they have webbed, bat-like wings and fins. it is likely that they were part of a set of altar vessels, for a number of similar examples are known, some bearing inscriptions. before being exported to europe, the pair of vases had probably stood for hundreds of years on a temple altar in china. this magnificent mid-ming period blue and white vase is actually one of a pair, its companion piece being owned by the musée guimet in paris. such sets were also made in bronze, although from early times pottery was substituted for metal. the lotus panel around the foot, the cloud collar on the shoulder and the plantain leaves on the neck and handles are further indicators of such a dating. the most interesting section comprises the band around the body, which has a lively design of dragons with flaming pearls above waves.
描述_ZN: 到了明朝中期，各种新的龙型开始出现在中国艺术中。 壶身良好，巧妙地用浅色、清澈的钴蓝色作画，这个花瓶的形式在1500年左右就已出现。 龙是不寻常的，因为它们有蹼、蝙蝠般的翅膀和鳍。 它们很可能是一套祭坛器皿的一部分，因为有许多类似的例子是已知的，有些还有铭文。 在出口到欧洲之前，这对花瓶可能已经在中国的一个寺庙祭坛上站了几百年了。 这个宏伟的明代中期青花瓶实际上是一对中的一个，它的同伴由巴黎的吉美博物馆拥有。 这种器皿也是用青铜制作的，尽管从早期开始就用陶器代替了金属。 足部的莲花图案、肩部的云纹座、颈部和把手的芭蕉叶都是这种年代的进一步标志。 最有趣的部分是围绕身体的带子，它有一个生动的龙的设计，上面有火焰珍珠的波浪。
